media.title: NBA Pressure Draft with JE Skeets | Slam N Jam
media.description: Who has the most pressure this NBA Season? Andrew Schlecht and Alex Speers are joined by JE Skeets of No Dunks to answer that question. Which All Star, Young Player, Playoff Team, Front Office and Wild card has the most pressure on them this season. Then the guys finish with another round of Andrew vs. the Beat.  00:00 Intro  01:20 Which NBA players and teams are under the most pressure? 02:32 Joel Embiid faces a now-or-never season in Philadelphia 05:09 Chet Holmgren has something to prove against San Antonio 09:10 De’Aaron Fox faces pressure with Dylan Harper waiting 11:50 Can the Magic escape another early playoff exit? 14:18 The Nuggets’ shrinking depth puts pressure on their title hopes 19:49 Can the Suns build on last season’s surprising progress? 23:11 Walker Kessler faces major expectations with the Lakers 24:52 Amen Thompson needs to take another offensive leap 28:15 Jalen Duren looks to bounce back from a rough postseason 30:40 Did the Celtics make the right call breaking up their core? 32:15 Tim Connelly’s big swings put pressure on the Timberwolves 36:42 The Wizards need to show their rebuild is working 42:36 Adam Silver faces mounting pressure around the NBA 45:36 Who can replace Mitchell Robinson as the Knicks’ backup center? 46:49 Pressure is on at Oklahoma City’s newly remodeled Braum’s 48:42 Can both Trail Blazers mascots survive under Tom Dundon? 54:38 Trivia: NBA players who never dunked    Full Episodes Playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLEuhZTLf0SW9N9etjaRh-KK7zRgKUOQ9l  Shorts Playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLEuhZTLf0SW8NBkdA2krD_sHQfI7Uhn4r

items.title: Before Kawhi, there was Wilt: In 1965, Chamberlain re-signed with the 76ers, with a secret verbal provision from Sixers ownership that Wilt would gain a significant portion of team ownership after he retired if he stayed. The owner died, his replacement refused to honor it, and Wilt demanded a trade
items.author: Known-Peak212
items.body_excerpt: It was verbal, rather than written, because it was against league rules for an active player to own a percentage of a team. Wilt tried to get around it by gaining up to 25% ownership of the Sixers after his playing career. Obviously, by the end of his life, that would have been…
